# Summary of Cairn System Rules

## Rule C1: Single Pulse
A pulse causes a cairn to grow. The growth amount equals the stride plus a bonus. The bonus equals how many complete stride-sized chunks fit into the current height (using integer division). Taller cairns with more complete strides grow faster.

## Rule C2: Repeated Pulses
Each pulse must be calculated independently using the height at that moment. You cannot reuse the bonus count from the first pulse for subsequent pulses—each one gets a fresh calculation based on the new height. This creates accelerating growth as cairns get taller.

## Rule C3: Leak (Single Pulse with Loss)
After a pulse is applied, if a cairn has a leak, it loses marks based on the new pulsed height. The number of marks lost equals the integer division of the new height by the leak size. The leak can sometimes cause a cairn to shrink despite gaining from the pulse.

## Rule C4: Finding Origin Height
To work backwards from a final height through pulses, you must reverse-engineer each pulse one at a time. Testing candidate starting heights by applying the correct number of pulses forward is an effective approach.

## Rule C5: Drain Cycles
A drain involves repeated cycles of pulse-then-remove-fixed-amount. The cairn doesn't empty quickly because pulses keep boosting it even as the drain removes marks. Finding when it reaches zero requires tracking multiple cycles.

## Rule C6: Merging Cairns
Two cairns combine into one using shares (proportions), floor operations, and a tether value. The tether contributes bonus marks based on the shorter cairn's size. Different tethers produce different results even with identical shares.
